title: Duck Confit
subtitle: French slow-cooked duck legs preserved in duck fat
excerpt: The great French preservation technique as a recipe: duck legs slow-cooked in their own fat at a very low temperature until the meat is falling-tender and the skin crisps to a shattering golden shell when finished in a hot pan.

recipe.sourceNotes: Confit (from the French confire, 'to preserve') is a technique of slow-cooking meat in its own rendered fat at a very low temperature (80 to 90°C), then storing it submerged in the same fat where it keeps for weeks or months. Duck confit originated in the Gascony region of south-west France as a preservation method before refrigeration. The leg is first cured in salt and aromatic herbs for several hours to draw out moisture, then cooked very slowly in duck fat. The result is meat of extraordinary tenderness, almost falling from the bone, with concentrated duck flavour. The preserved confit legs are finished by frying skin-side down in a very hot pan until the skin crisps; this rendering step removes the excess fat and produces the characteristic shattering, golden skin.

content.text: The oven temperature is critical: 90°C (conventional) keeps the fat below simmering. Any higher and the fat will boil, which fries rather than confit the duck and produces a tougher result. The overnight salt cure is important; do not skip it. The crisping step at the end requires a dry, very hot pan and patience; do not move the duck for the first 5 minutes.

items.preparation: enough to submerge the legs; tinned duck fat

content.text: Rub the duck legs all over with the salt, pepper, thyme, garlic, and crumbled bay. Refrigerate uncovered for at least 12 hours (overnight is standard).

Preheat the oven to 90°C (conventional) / 80°C fan. Wipe the cure from the legs. Melt the duck fat in an ovenproof pot. Add the legs, completely submerged. Cook for 2 to 2.5 hours until the meat yields easily when pierced. Cool in the fat. (Can be stored in the fat in the fridge for up to 4 weeks at this point.)

To serve: remove the legs from the fat and wipe off excess fat. Place skin-side down in a cold dry frying pan. Turn the heat to medium-high. Fry for 8 to 10 minutes, undisturbed, until the skin is deeply golden and shattering-crisp. Turn briefly to warm the meat side through. Serve with lentils, white beans, or frisée salad.
